code_first.code:
attempts = 4
if attempts > 3 then
    print("Alert")
endif
p: Explain the first assignment or condition that determines the output.
Extend to lock an account after three failed attempts.
code_first.a: Alert; no output for 3; use attempts >= 3.

original_exam_questions: Give the meaning of phishing. [2 marks]
Deceptive communication designed to trick a user into disclosing data or taking unsafe actions.
Explain how ransomware can harm a school. [3 marks]
Malware may encrypt/deny access to files, disrupt services and cause recovery costs.
Name one precaution against social engineering. [2 marks]
Staff training, verifying requests independently or multifactor authentication.

optional_original_challenge.coreHint: With attempts=4 and the test >3, the alert appears.

stretch.task: Change the logic so the alert appears at three failures, not four.
stretch.answer: At attempts=3 it now prints Alert.

mastery.task: Simulate repeated login attempts using a loop: stop at a correct password or lock after three failures. Test the third-attempt boundary.
mastery.hint: Keep a counter; check success and limit separately.
mastery.answer: Three failures -> Locked; two failures then correct -> success; counter increments only on failure. Never display the stored secret.
